subject: Re: Dedicated commit sizing — GPU prioritization framework
messages:
From: Maya Chen <maya@veridianai.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 29 Jul 2027 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated sizing question for upcoming commit

Hi Rishi,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. We're kicking off procurement for a Dedicated deployment and need a sizing recommendation to include in our procurement pack. High-level: we plan to serve Llama3-xl with context windows up to 64k tokens for long-form summarization plus a smaller set of shorter-chat models for interactive features. Peak qps is estimated at 120 concurrent active users (tail-heavy), average response length ~800 tokens.

The questions we have:
- Memory vs latency: given the 64k context work, should we prioritize H100 (memory) or A100 (cost/perf)?
- Can L4 be a cost-saving tier for short-context traffic?
- Any suggested baseline slot counts and a recommended burst/fallback strategy?

We'd like a short rationale so our procurement team can justify the SKU mix.

Appreciate the guidance,
Maya
Maya Chen | Head of Platform Engineering
VeridianAI

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Chen <maya@veridianai.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Jul 2027 17:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing question for upcoming commit

Hi Maya — thanks for the context, this is helpful. Short answer up front: prioritize H100 for baseline capacity when long-context (64k) residency and large KV caches are common; use A100 as the predictable throughput/burst tier; L4 is a strong cost-tier for short-context interactive paths but not for your long-context summarization.

Rationale (concise):
- H100: much larger HBMe and attention memory; better for single-request large-context residency (fewer OOMs) and reduces need for complex tile/tiling logic. Higher per-hour cost but fewer engineering fallbacks.
- A100: good balance for high qps short-to-medium contexts; higher throughput per dollar for many parallel short requests. Use as burst/backfill when H100 slots are saturated.
- L4: excellent for low-latency short responses and embedding/utility routes. Avoid for 64k-resident workloads; too many cross-device KV swaps.

Suggested baseline (quick sketch):
- Baseline reserved: 8 x H100 nodes (for steady-state long-context workers + KV cache capacity).
- Burst pool: 16 x A100 nodes (autoscaled, reserved-burst bucket) to handle spikes and high qps short-path traffic.
- Edge/low-cost: 12 x L4 fractional nodes (cost-optimized pool for interactive chat & embedding endpoints).

Next steps: I attached a draft proposal and a capacity worksheet with simple perf assumptions. If you're OK, I'll loop in our ops/product folks to confirm slot-sizing and fallback latency SLOs.

Attachments: veridian-dedicated-proposal-draft.pdf
Drive: https://drive.redwood.com/rdw/RDW-4721/proposal

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference

Date: Fri, 30 Jul 2027 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: INTERNAL: Veridian RDW-4721 — confirm GPU prioritization and sizing

Team — Maya at Veridian (cc: ops-prod) asked for a short rationale and concrete slot counts to include in procurement. I sketched a baseline (8 H100 / 16 A100 burst / 12 L4 edge). Need ops/tiling input and confirmation that we can meet a 99th pct latency SLO for the long-context path with 8 H100 given their expected QPS shape.

Quick perf assumptions I used in the worksheet (attached capacity-worksheet.csv):
- Llama3-xl @ 64k: ~1.3 tokens/ms on H100, KV residency per slot = 400GB effective context split (approx); concurrent long-context active workers per H100 = ~6 (sustained inference, optimistic).
- A100 (40GB): well-suited for short requests: ~2.2 tokens/ms per card for 2k contexts when batched; good throughput for burst.
- L4 (24GB): ~3.5 tokens/ms for short-chat (<=2k), but lacks headroom for 64k.

Questions for ops:
1) Can we validate the concurrent long-context workers per H100 estimate (6) vs your telemetry?
2) Ops fallback: what is realistic cold-start and cross-device KV penalty if we move long-context requests to A100 during H100 saturation?
3) Any infra constraints for reserving 8 H100 today (regional availability in us-west2)?

If we agree, I'll produce a single-slide rationale for procurement and a short SOW bullet list (SLA, pricing bands, commitment term).

Attachments: capacity-worksheet.csv

Thanks,
Rishi

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 30 Jul 2027 11:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: INTERNAL: Veridian RDW-4721 — confirm GPU prioritization and sizing

Rishi — quick ops readout after scanning the worksheet and querying capacity:
- Concurrent long-context workers per H100: realistic steady-state is closer to 4–5 based on current KV cache residency telemetry (we see heavy tail and some sticky sessions that push the concurrency down). Plan for 5 to be conservative.
- Cross-device KV fallback cost: moving a 64k request to A100 introduces a ~2.5–3x latency multiplier in practice due to networked KV chunking and additional serialization; not ideal for latency-sensitive summarization. Works as temporary backfill but degrades P75/P95 noticeably.
- Regional availability: us-west2 has limited H100 spare capacity this quarter. We can provision 6 immediately; additional 2 would be a 3–6 week lead depending on stock or we can hybrid-reserve 6 H100 + 2 H100-equivalents in colocated partner pool (billing slightly different).

Ops recommendation:
- Set Baseline reserved = 6 H100 in us-west2 + 2 H100-equivalents in partner pool (total 8 logical). Communicate hybrid lead times to procurement.
- Keep A100 burst pool at 16 nodes; configure automatic routing policy: prefer H100 for any request >8k tokens, failover to A100 only when H100 queue latency exceeds X ms.
- L4: target for short-path routes only; plan for separate autoscaling policy and lower memory limits.

I'm attaching our fallback playbook excerpt for procurement language.

Attachments: ops-fallback-playbook.md

Irene
Director, Dedicated Operations

Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing question for upcoming commit — proposed baseline and procurement language

Hi Maya — thanks for the patience while I confirmed with ops. Below is a concise recommendation you can drop into procurement along with the attached draft proposal and worksheet. Let me know if you want this turned into a one-page SOW fragment.

Executive recommendation (summary):
- Baseline reserved capacity: 6 x H100 (us-west2) + 2 x H100-equivalents in partner pool (logical total = 8 H100). Rationale: H100 is necessary to host 64k KV residency with acceptable latency and to reduce engineering complexity and risk. Ops availability drives the hybrid mix.
- Burst/backfill: 16 x A100 (autoscaling pool). Use for high-concurrency short-to-medium context traffic and as a controlled burst tier when H100 queueing occurs. Expect some latency inflation for 64k work if moved to A100 — use as planned backfill only.
- Cost-tier / Edge: L4 pool (12 fractional nodes) for interactive chat and embedding endpoints where short-context latency and cost-per-token are the priority.

Procurement-friendly bullets to include in SOW/commit:
- Commitment: 12-month Dedicated commitment with tiered pricing: baseline H100 monthly fee + burst A100 effective hourly pricing.
- SLA: 99.5% availability for baseline reserved pool; fallback routing policy documented and tested quarterly.
- Lead times & hybrid plan: 6 H100 immediate, additional 2 via partner pool with expected 3–6 week provisioning window.

Next steps:
1) If this looks good, we can finalize the numbers into the SOW and our legal/procurement templates.
2) Please review the attached PDF (veridian-dedicated-proposal-draft.pdf) and the capacity worksheet; I included the ops fallback playbook excerpt for procurement language.
